Priya: FYI I hit a stale-prefix read during an eviction-heavy window. putting notes here so we can decide a guardrail.
Marco: quick summary?
Priya: sequence: prefetch cached header -> eviction/compaction on host frees segment ids -> concurrent read tries to decode header -> segment miss -> fallback to remote replica which returned older data. End result: client saw v1 while v2 already committed.
Olga: classic reclamation vs cache pointer mismatch. two immediate levers: 1) attach a lightweight ‘compact_epoch’ to headers and validate on hit, 2) make compaction delay reclamation until caches TTL out.
Sam: compact_epoch compare is cheap iff we maintain per-tenant epoch locally. broadcast on compaction event; nodes keep cached compact_epoch TTLed. comparison is integer check on hot path.
Priya: downside: broadcast storm for high-churn tenants. but we can sample checks or only validate when the decoder hits a local fetch 404. That keeps common path fast.
Marco: also consider a one-shot fence increment on handoff/compaction that we piggyback on existing gossip channel (no extra sequencer writes). cheap to implement.
Olga: we should add metrics first: prefetched_segment_404.count, prefetched_gen_mismatch.count, fallback_to_remote.count. Without numbers we can’t pick.
Sam: rollout plan: add gen-compare guarded by FF, enable sampling 2% first, canary on one shard. add latency buckets for validated hits.
Priya: agree. I’ll author the harness that simulates tight write+compact cycles and produce numbers. Marco can add metrics & FF.
agent-bot: feature-flag created: prefetched_gen_check; canary rollout scheduled 2024-08-01T03:00:00Z.
Priya: next: run harness, gather metrics, then choose gen-compare (preferred) vs lazy GC if disk pressure is acceptable. Will post results here. :rocket:
